steps.text: Stir together ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, mustard powder, garlic powder, and pepper in a small bowl until well combined. Cover and refrigerate before serving to blend flavors, at least 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Tonkatsu / Katsu Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Try katsu sauce with this simple five-ingredient recipe made with pantry staples and served with deep-fried breaded pork or chicken cutlets.
raw_recipe.name: Tonkatsu / Katsu Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Stir together ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, mustard powder, garlic powder, and pepper in a small bowl until well combined. Cover and refrigerate before serving to blend flavors, at least 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: Excellent. What I like about this sauce is exactly the thing a couple of people tweaked out - it's not sweet. Unsolicited, my 20yo said, "This sauce is incredibly good and spicy." Well said, I think. Thanks for the recipe! :) UPDATE: I don't make a lot of recipes more than once because I'm an adventurer, but I have visited this recipe a few times since I first made it. I made it again tonight for fish katsu and was out of garlic powder so I used fresh - still excellent. I've also used this sauce on steamed shrimp - makes an awesome cocktail sauce. Thanks again!

I made half the recipe, and it was the perfect amount for us. I used slightly less pepper and used half garlic, half onion powders. The longer you let this sit the better it is. When I tried it right after mixing, the ketchup and pepper taste was overwhelming. After sitting in the fridge for a few hours the flavours mellowed out a bit and were more balanced. Yum!

I just paired this with tonkatsu for dinner and it was ok. The only thing that I don't like is that the pepper taste is too strong Probably I'll tone it down to 3/4 tsp next time just like what I did to the garlic powder. Adding 3/4 tsp onion powder makes it good. And also not to mention, I also added a little bit of sugar as what other reviewers mentioned. Thank you Soifua =)

I didn't follow the recipe exactly. I eyeballed other ingredients which I believe is essential to Tonkatsu sauce. Measuring to taste: I added a few teaspoons of shoyu (soy sauce), 1-2 teaspoon of sugar, and about 1-2 tablespoons of applesauce. I cut down on the ketchup, about 1/2 cup and added more Worcestershire, about 1/4 cup or less. Over all, the sauce came to 1 cup for me. But the applesauce is important. Why? Because a lot of bottled tonkatsu sauces have fruit in it, like apple, dates, etc. Now, for a hint of spice, I add a light sprinkle of cinnamon. I used yours as a basis, but being that I eyeballed the rest, I can't really post up my own version. :) Remember, really good tonkatsu has some apple in it!
perfect as written. I used mustard seed and crushed in my mortar to add more texture.

Having never had chicken Katsu myself, i made this for my boyfriend who loves it. I made this sauce and also purchased a packaged sauce from the store for comparison. This recipe won, hands down!! the store bought sauce just tasted like ketchup and Worcestershire sauce and was runny. This one is spicy, and intense and flavorful! It does pack some kick so if you don't like the heat, maybe lessen the black pepper and mustard, but I wouldn't change a thing! I did use fresh garlic (about 3 cloves) instead of the powder, but other than that followed the recipe exactly. It does get hotter over time as well. I plan to bake some meatballs with this sauce for a spicy asian take on bbq meatballs...thanks for the recipe!!

I added 1/2 Cup of sugar and 1t of pepper, I cooked until it was hot and the sugar mixed in. I think next time next time I will use even less pepper, it was HOT and I'm a wimp. But it was still yummy.
This sauce tasted primarily of Worcestershire sauce. Perhaps if you add the Worcestershire in increments, tasting as you go, you will find the right blend, but we thought it was just OK as written.
It goes really well with Chicken Katsu. I use fresh garlic instead of powder (or both), and add some soy sauce, but leave it alone other than that.
Was very good with chicken Katsu recipe I made from this site. I used prepared mustard (4T) since I had no powder. Tasty, actually a little too hot for me but my husband liked it a lot

I made this tonight to go with fried calamari steaks and it was very good; I added about 1/4 cup chicken broth to make it less bold. I also used just 1/2 tsp of the spices and it was perfect for our taste... The hubby really liked it and I'm anxious to try it on other things like chicken. Thanks for the great recipe! :)
This is a very tasty sauce. It’s good on many different things.
Terrible, this taste like ketchup and black pepper.
too mustardy tasting but i did have to sub prepared mustard for dry.. :(
This is good! It's pretty much just a barbecue sauce, like one commenter said, but I like it a lot.

i only used half the amount of ketchup needed because for one I was low on ketchup. maybe this is why it didn't quite turn out right. it was more of a BBQ sauce to me. a really good one but not necessarily what i was looking for. could have been all the Worcestershire sauce.
Didn't and wouldn't change a thing!!!
It was too thick, and to peppery, not what I've had at teriyaki joints.

I really wanted to like this recipe. I just didn't. It didn't taste anything like katsu sauce. Totally dominated by the flavor of the ketchup. Texture was also really weird. Oh well, I'll just go back to buying Bulldog brand sauce.
We didn't care for this sauce at all. Sorry.
